name: Password stored in plaintext
description:
The application stores user passwords in a recoverable form and returns them from its own records. Anyone who can read the store (a database dump, a backup, an injection flaw, an insider) obtains every password directly, and because users reuse passwords the impact reaches other systems.

burpsy reports this only on proof: a replayed request with working credentials answered with JSON in which a member other than the password parameter's own name holds the submitted password verbatim, while the same request with a random marker in place of the password answered with neither the marker nor the original password, so the field is not simply echoed back.

This row is burpsy's own: Burp's issue catalogue has no entry for it.
remediation: Never store passwords in plaintext or with reversible encryption or encoding. Store a salted, deliberately slow password hash (Argon2id, scrypt, bcrypt or PBKDF2) and compare against it. Never return a password, or its hash, to the client.

vulnerabilityClassifications.title: CWE-256: Plaintext Storage of a Password
